Let \(V=\mathbb F_p^8\), so \(R=\operatorname{End}_{\mathbb F_p}(V)\). Fix a nonsquare \(\varepsilon\in\mathbb F_p^\times\).

Every subfield \(E\subset R\) of order \(p^2\) makes \(V\) a \(4\)-dimensional vector space over \(E\). Hence for \(a\in E\),
\[
\operatorname{tr}_{R}(a)=4\operatorname{Tr}_{E/\mathbb F_p}(a).
\]
Since \(p\) is odd, this is zero exactly when \(\operatorname{Tr}_{E/\mathbb F_p}(a)=0\). The trace-zero elements of \(E\) form a \(1\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-space, say \(\mathbb F_p X\), and for \(X\ne0\),
\[
X^2\in\mathbb F_p^\times
\]
is a nonsquare. Conversely, such an \(X\) generates \(E=\mathbb F_p[X]\).

Thus each field \(E_i\) is represented by a line \(\mathbb F_p X_i\), and the condition is exactly
\[
X_iX_j=-X_jX_i.
\]
After rescaling each \(X_i\), we may choose representatives \(J_i\) satisfying
\[
J_i^2=\varepsilon I,\qquad J_iJ_j=-J_jJ_i.
\]
Each field gives exactly two such choices, \(J_i\) and \(-J_i\), so the desired count is the number of ordered signed \(7\)-tuples \((J_1,\dots,J_7)\) divided by \(2^7\).

Let \(C\) be the \(\mathbb F_p\)-algebra generated by \(e_1,\dots,e_7\) with relations
\[
e_i^2=\varepsilon,\qquad e_ie_j=-e_je_i\quad(i\ne j).
\]
The element
\[
\omega=e_1e_2\cdots e_7
\]
is central, and
\[
\omega^2=(-1)^{21}\varepsilon^7=-\varepsilon^7.
\]
Since \(\varepsilon^6\) is a square, the square class of \(\omega^2\) is that of \(-\varepsilon\).

If \(p\equiv1\pmod4\), then \(-1\) is a square, so \(-\varepsilon\) is a nonsquare. Then \(C\) has center \(\mathbb F_{p^2}\) and is isomorphic to \(M_8(\mathbb F_{p^2})\) as an \(\mathbb F_p\)-algebra. It has no unital representation on an \(8\)-dimensional \(\mathbb F_p\)-space, since its \(\mathbb F_p\)-dimension is \(128>64=\dim_{\mathbb F_p}M_8(\mathbb F_p)\). Hence the count is \(0\).

If \(p\equiv3\pmod4\), then \(-1\) is a nonsquare, so \(-\varepsilon\) is a square. Then
\[
C\cong M_8(\mathbb F_p)\oplus M_8(\mathbb F_p).
\]
A signed ordered \(7\)-tuple \((J_1,\dots,J_7)\) is the same as a unital algebra homomorphism
\[
C\to M_8(\mathbb F_p).
\]
Such a homomorphism must project onto one of the two simple factors and then apply an automorphism of \(M_8(\mathbb F_p)\). The automorphism group is \(\operatorname{PGL}_8(\mathbb F_p)\), of size
\[
|\operatorname{PGL}_8(\mathbb F_p)|
=\frac{|GL_8(\mathbb F_p)|}{p-1}.
\]
There are two choices of simple factor, so the number of signed tuples is
\[
2\frac{|GL_8(\mathbb F_p)|}{p-1}.
\]
Dividing by \(2^7\) gives
\[
\frac{|GL_8(\mathbb F_p)|}{64(p-1)}.
\]
Using
\[
|GL_8(\mathbb F_p)|=\prod_{k=0}^{7}(p^8-p^k),
\]
the required number is
\[
\boxed{
\begin{cases}
0,& p\equiv1\pmod4,\\[4pt]
\dfrac{1}{64(p-1)}\displaystyle\prod_{k=0}^{7}(p^8-p^k),& p\equiv3\pmod4.
\end{cases}}
\]
